title: Kedukan Bukit inscription
description: The oldest dated record of Srivijaya, the sea power that controlled the Strait of Malacca for centuries, is carved in Old Malay.

title: Borobudur completed
description: The Sailendra rulers of central Java finish the largest Buddhist monument in the world.

title: Prambanan built
description: The Hindu temple complex of Prambanan is begun a few miles from Borobudur.

title: Chola raid on Srivijaya
description: A fleet sent by Rajendra Chola of southern India sacks Srivijaya's ports and weakens its hold on the straits.

title: Mongol invasion of Java
description: Raden Wijaya uses and then expels an invading Yuan army and founds Majapahit, the last great Hindu-Buddhist empire of the islands.

title: Nagarakretagama written
description: A court poem describes Majapahit at its height under Hayam Wuruk and lists dependencies across the archipelago.

title: Portuguese reach the Spice Islands
description: A year after taking Malacca the Portuguese reach the source of cloves and nutmeg.

title: Demak overruns Majapahit
description: The Muslim sultanate of Demak conquers what remains of Majapahit, marking the turn of Java to Islam.

title: First Dutch fleet at Banten
description: Cornelis de Houtman's ships reach the pepper port of Banten, opening the Dutch trade with the islands.

title: Conquest of the Banda Islands
description: Jan Pieterszoon Coen kills or deports most of the Bandanese to give the Company a monopoly of nutmeg.

title: Sultan Agung besieges Batavia
description: The ruler of Mataram twice fails to take the Dutch headquarters on Java.

title: Treaty of Bongaya
description: The sultanate of Gowa submits to the Company, which takes control of the trade of Makassar.

title: Batavia massacre
description: Company soldiers and townspeople kill about ten thousand ethnic Chinese residents.

title: Treaty of Giyanti
description: Mataram is divided between the courts of Surakarta and Yogyakarta, both dependent on the Company.

title: British invasion of Java
description: British forces take Java during the Napoleonic Wars and Stamford Raffles governs it until it is returned to the Dutch in 1816.

title: Eruption of Tambora
description: The largest eruption in recorded history kills tens of thousands and causes the 'year without a summer' across the northern hemisphere.

title: Java War
description: Prince Diponegoro leads the last great Javanese resistance to Dutch rule, at a cost of about 200,000 lives.

title: Cultivation System introduced
description: Javanese villages are made to grow export crops for the government, which becomes a main source of Dutch state income.

title: Aceh War begins
description: The Dutch invade Aceh and fight for three decades to subdue it.

title: Eruption of Krakatoa
description: The island explodes and the tsunamis that follow kill more than 36,000 people.

title: Budi Utomo founded
description: Medical students found the first native political society, the date kept as the day of national awakening.

title: Youth Pledge
description: A congress of youth groups declares one homeland, one nation and one language, Indonesian.

title: Dutch surrender to Japan
description: The Dutch forces capitulate after a campaign of three months, ending Dutch rule in practice.

title: Proclamation of independence
description: Two days after Japan's surrender Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta declare Indonesia independent.

title: Battle of Surabaya
description: British troops take the city from republican fighters after three weeks, a battle remembered as Heroes' Day.

title: Bandung Conference
description: Leaders of 29 Asian and African states meet to oppose colonialism and stand apart from the Cold War blocs.

title: Guided Democracy
description: Sukarno dissolves the constitutional assembly by decree and restores the 1945 constitution with a strong presidency.

title: 30 September Movement
description: Six generals are killed in a failed coup blamed on the Communist Party, and the army under Suharto answers with killings of at least half a million people.

title: Suharto takes the presidency
description: The assembly removes Sukarno and names General Suharto acting president, beginning the New Order.

title: Invasion of East Timor
description: Indonesia invades the former Portuguese colony days after it declared independence, beginning a 24-year occupation.

title: Suharto resigns
description: After the Asian financial crisis, student protests and riots, Suharto steps down after 31 years and democratic reform begins.

title: East Timor votes for independence
description: In a referendum run by the United Nations 78 percent reject autonomy within Indonesia; militias lay waste to the territory before peacekeepers arrive.

title: Bali bombings
description: Bombs set by the Islamist group Jemaah Islamiyah kill 202 people, most of them foreign tourists.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami
description: An earthquake off Sumatra sends waves around the ocean, killing about 230,000 people, more than half of them in Aceh.
